cards.title: Why Birth Rates Are Plummeting and Why It Matters
cards.body: Author Camilla Cavendish explores the many reasons people are having fewer children, from dating apps to unaffordable housing and climate concerns. Understanding these trends helps parents and policymakers address the insecurity preventing families from forming.

cards.title: I Went to Ikea With My Son: Parenting Failures
cards.body: A parent discovers how much domestic wisdom they've imparted to their child during a pre-university shopping trip. The experience highlights what kids actually learn from their parents about life skills.

cards.title: When Your Needs and Your Child's Needs Are at Odds
cards.body: Sometimes what your child needs from you and what you need don't align. It's okay to prioritize your own wellbeing sometimes.

cards.title: How Do You Help a Child With ADHD Be Happy?
cards.body: Kids with ADHD can flourish by focusing on their strengths while addressing challenges. This approach helps them thrive rather than just cope.

cards.title: When Kindness Meets Hate: What Parents Can Teach Children
cards.body: Help kids understand difficult emotions, resist antisemitism and hate, and practice empathy, courage, and compassion over cruelty. These lessons build stronger, more resilient young people.

cards.title: The Self-Aware Sports Parent
cards.body: Youth sports can bring out the best—and stress—in kids and parents. Learn what belongs to you, what belongs to them, and help kids know they're more than their sport.

cards.title: PowerBars and Other Signs the Empty Nest Is Coming
cards.body: Preparing emotionally for your kids to leave for college is a journey. Recognizing the small signs helps you navigate this major life transition.

cards.title: How Children Learn Best
cards.body: Research shows how students learn most effectively, and the answer is surprisingly intuitive. Understanding these principles helps parents support their child's education at home.

cards.title: What Makes Trauma Survivors 'Turn Out Well'?
cards.body: Resilience isn't about avoiding hardship—it's about breaking cycles of trauma. Understanding what helps survivors thrive offers hope for families facing adversity.
